_meta.what: Which terms on TripSit's combination axis may be read as one of Piru's DrugClass values.
_meta.why: TripSit's matrix mixes classes with substances. 'benzodiazepines' is a class; 'ketamine', 'lsd' and 'mephedrone' are not, and reading a ketamine-specific note as a claim about every dissociative invents one — TripSit's lithium warning names MXE, its pregabalin seizure warning names NBOMe, and its MAOI warning names αMT. Only a term that IS the class it maps to, or is TripSit's own class term, is listed. Everything else is dropped rather than generalised; the loss is real and it is the honest side to err on.
_meta.severity: TripSit's six statuses collapse onto Piru's three. The distinction between 'Low Risk & Synergy' and 'Low Risk & Decrease' — opposite advice at the same severity — survives in `interaction_rules.status`, which is stored verbatim.
_meta.curated_wins: Where a pair already has a hand-written Swift rule, that rule wins. TripSit is community consensus; the Swift rules carry adjudications that deliberately contradict folk ordering (MDMA + SSRI is blockade, not danger).
